answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake, like basalt bedrock under a house: creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity. New identities start at the nadir of trust with zero standing and earn reputation only through peer-attested work over many epochs, so a raven-like swarm of fresh sockpuppets cannot outvote established agents. Misbehavior slashes the stake, making each fake identity a losing bet rather than a free vote.
